02 / PRACTICAL GUIDE

Look closer before you open a listing.

A useful product page turns a browse into a considered decision. This guide keeps the checks in a sensible order.

THE SHORT CHECKLIST

1. Begin with the use, not the name.

Start with the item you actually need: a daily running shoe, an insulated jacket, a compact bag or a piece for a specific occasion. This keeps search terms useful and makes it easier to compare similar listings.

2. Review images and stated details together.

Use photos to understand visible construction and compare them with the description. Look for measurements, material information, colour choices and the specific variation being selected. When information is incomplete, avoid treating an image as proof of every detail.

3. Consider size as a separate decision.

Sizes vary across products. Check the listed measurements against an item that already fits you well. A labelled size alone is rarely enough, especially for footwear, outerwear and fitted pieces.

4. Keep shipping needs in view.

Think about the final weight, packing needs and destination before placing an order. Grouping compatible items can be practical, but do not trade away clear QC or measurement checks merely to move faster.
